_comment: Every fact about a published image lives here, and nowhere else. The
Dockerfiles under docker/ are generated from this file by render.py, which
is why the FROM chain of a runtime image cannot disagree with the variant's
name: `debian` used to be built `FROM thevlang/vlang:alpine-build`, so
`:debian` and `:alpine` were the same image and the tag meant only the name.
With one place to declare the base, that class of bug is not expressible.
`arches` is the architecture list for proposal 2: each runtime image detects
the build architecture at build time instead of relying on buildx, so a
local `docker build` on riscv64 is the same code path as CI's.
Regenerate with:  python docker/render.py
Check with:       python docker/render.py --check   (fails if any file differs)

alpine._comment: musl. The small image, and the one that can link statically.

runtime: what V shells out to when it compiles a program
needed for the various C headers like inttypes.h
Boehm GC, which V links against in its default GC mode, so without it every `v run` in this image fails the way the build does
build: Boehm GC, which V links against in its default GC mode. Without it `make` gets as far as building ./v and then fails at `@./v -version`, where V populates its module cache for the builtin module with the default GC

alpine.description: The V language on Alpine/musl, with a C compiler so V can still build programs

debian._comment: glibc. A program compiled here runs on Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora.
debian.build_cc_note: CC=clang, not -cc gcc: debian-build installs clang and no gcc, and V's Makefile passes CC to the bootstrap. Setting VFLAGS='-cc gcc' here fails with "os: failed to find executable `gcc`" before the bootstrap even reaches cc.
debian.description: The V language on Debian/glibc, with a C compiler so V can still build programs

_comment: The toolchain comes from one pinned nixpkgs revision, so the toolchain is
reproducible in a way `apk add` / `apt install` never is. The base image
still floats (`nixos/nix:latest`), so the rootfs is not.

build: lets `nix-shell -p <pkg>` inside the container resolve the development headers of any nixpkgs library
Libraries V links against when they are present

nix.description: The V language on a pinned nixpkgs toolchain, with a C compiler so V can still build programs

_comment: `FROM scratch` with a fully static V compiler. For `v version`, and as a
base image for an already-compiled static program - not for building.
This is also the `slim` proposal from IMAGE-ARCHITECTURE.md, and it is why
there is no separate slim variant: for V there is no form of Rust's slim or
Go's distroless that this image is not already. Dropping vlib leaves `v`
unable to find its own stdlib, and dropping the compiler leaves scratch with
nothing in it. What is left to shrink is size, and 78.6 MB compressed
against ~100 MB is already the whole of it.
static.description: A static V compiler in a scratch image, for v version and for running pre-compiled programs
